perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s perspective, the information available to her is:

- I am Sara Manuelito, a Speech-Language Pathologist and American Indian.  
- I know Shirley Whiteplume as my long-time nurse colleague and close friend at the community health center. We have worked together for years.

What I directly experienced, observed, heard, said, or knew:

- I attended the funeral of our mutual patient. I saw Shirley looking somber and suspected she was deeply affected by the loss.
- I told Shirley I knew this was hard for her and that I saw how much she cared for him.
- Shirley told me it had been tough, that she kept thinking there was something more we could have done, and that it was hard to let go.
- I told her we did everything we could, that we should remember the good care and moments of joy we brought into his life. Shirley said I was right.

- During a coffee break at work, I brought up our treatment decisions because I sensed she felt burdened by the outcome.
- Shirley said she felt responsible, wondered if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance, and said it was hard to accept.
- I told her we made the best decisions with the information we had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. She said she appreciated that.

- In our office, after seeing Shirley’s continued reserved behavior and minimal emotional expression, I told her I noticed she was holding back and that it was okay to be open.
- Shirley said she was not sure she could, and that she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak.
- I told her showing emotions does not make her weak and that it is healthy to express them among friends. Shirley said maybe I was right and that she would try to be more open.

- Later, I felt my previous confrontation might have been too harsh, so I apologized if I came on too strong.
- Shirley said it was a bit much but that she knew I meant well, and she appreciated my apology.
- I told her I was there for her in whatever way she needed. Shirley said we should keep talking, because it helps.

- After some time, I noticed Shirley’s demeanor had improved and I felt hopeful. I asked how she was feeling.
- Shirley said she was feeling better thanks to our talks and my support.
- I suggested spending more time together outside of work. Shirley said she would like that and suggested planning something for the weekend.

I do not have access to Shirley’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she stated or what I observed and inferred from her behavior. I also do not know hidden events or narrator-only details unavailable to me.
